analysis.investment_thesis: Jyothy Labs is a decent consumer staples business with 24.6% ROCE and near-zero debt, but at an earnings yield of only ~5.7% (EBIT ₹500 Cr / EV ~₹8,736 Cr), it fails to clear the Magic Formula's cheapness bar. The Magic Formula demands both high ROIC AND a bargain price — here we only have one.
key_strengths: ROCE of 24.6% clears the 20% quality threshold — efficient capital deployment across multiple FMCG brands
Debt destruction: borrowings collapsed from ₹285 Cr (2020) to ₹61 Cr (2025), D/E now 0.04 — nearly debt-free
Operating leverage evident: EBITDA doubled from ₹266 Cr (2022) to ₹536 Cr (2025) on modest revenue growth
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 6.7% over 9 years is well below my preferred 10-15%+ threshold — this is a slow-growth business in competitive FMCG
Earnings yield of ~5.7% is below the 6% Magic Formula floor — no margin of safety at current price
FCF dropped sharply from ₹443 Cr (2024) to ₹254 Cr (2025) as investing outflows rose — capex and M&A appetite increasing
red_flags: Earnings yield ~5.7% fails Magic Formula cheapness threshold — stock is priced for perfection at 17.6x EV/EBITDA
Revenue growth at 6.7% CAGR suggests limited pricing power and market share gains despite multi-brand portfolio
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula numbers: EBIT of ₹500 Cr against an EV of roughly ₹8,736 Cr (market cap ₹8,752 Cr + debt ₹61 Cr − cash ₹77 Cr) gives an earnings yield of just 5.7% — below my 6% floor and far from the 12-15%+ that would make me excited. ROCE of 24.6% is respectable and clears my 20% quality bar, but not exceptional enough to justify paying a full price. The Magic Formula only works when you get quality AND cheapness together; here you're paying a fair-to-full price for a decent-but-not-great business.

The business fundamentals are solid but not special: near-zero debt is commendable, and the operating leverage from 2022-2024 is encouraging (EBITDA nearly doubled). However, 6.7% revenue CAGR over 9 years reveals a business growing roughly in line with nominal Indian GDP, not a share-gainer. The 12.87% operating margin, while improving, is modest for an FMCG player with 47.9% gross margins — significant overhead drag. At P/E of 23.9x and EV/EBITDA of 17.6x, Mr. Market has already priced in the margin improvement story. I'd want this at 12-14x EV/EBITDA (roughly ₹160-180 per share) before the Magic Formula lights up.
